facts.statement: Sebastian Apesteguía described Bonitasaura in 2004 based on a partial sub-adult skeleton found in fluvial sandstone.
facts.quote: The remains, consisting of a partial sub-adult skeleton jumbled in a small area of fluvial sandstone, including a lower jaw with teeth, a partial vertebrae series, and limb bones, were described by Sebastian Apesteguía in 2004.

facts.statement: The genus name Bonitasaura comes from the quarry name "La Bonita", and the species name salgadoi honors paleontologist Leonardo Salgado.
facts.quote: The genus name Bonitasaura refers to the fossil quarry's name, "La Bonita", while the name of the type species, B. salgadoi, pays homage to Leonardo Salgado, a renowned Argentine paleontologist.

facts.statement: Bonitasaura lived during the Late Cretaceous (Santonian) in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Río Negro Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Bonitasaura is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur hailing from uppermost layers of the Late Cretaceous (Santonian) Bajo de la Carpa Formation, Neuquén Group of the eastern Neuquén Basin, located in Río Negro Province, Northwestern Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: Bonitasaura measured 10 meters in length and possessed a skull similar to that of diplodocid sauropods.
facts.quote: Bonitasaura measured 10 m in length, and had a skull similar to another group of sauropods, the diplodocids.

facts.statement: The keratin sheath on Bonitasaura's jaw functioned like a guillotine to crop vegetation.
facts.quote: The keratin sheath worked much like a guillotine to crop vegetation raked into the mouth by the peg-like front teeth.

facts.statement: Bonitasaura had a short neck with robust vertebrae projections, suggesting it was used for vigorous feeding exertions.
facts.quote: This animal also had a rather short neck and robust projections of the back vertebrae for muscle attachment, indicating that the neck was used in vigorous exertions, probably during feeding.

facts.statement: The discovery of Bonitasaura suggests that Antarctosaurus is likely not a chimera of a titanosaurian body and a diplodocoid jaw.
facts.quote: It also made the suggestion that the titanosaur Antarctosaurus is a chimera made up of a titanosaurian skull and body and a diplodocoid jaw, as proposed by some authors (McIntosh 1990; Jacobs et al. 1993; Upchurch 1999) less likely.

facts.statement: Bonitasaura was originally classified in Nemegtosauridae but is now placed within the titanosaur clade including Lognkosauria and Rinconsauria.
facts.quote: Bonitasaura was originally classified as a member of Nemegtosauridae in the original description, but subsequent cladistic analyses and description found it to be nested among the titanosaur clade that includes Lognkosauria and Rinconsauria.

facts.statement: Agnolin et al. (2023) recovered Bonitasaura as a colossosaurian titanosaur and sister taxon to a clade containing Chucarosaurus, Notocolossus, and Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: In the description of Chucarosaurus in 2023, Agnolin et al. recovered Bonitasaura as a colossosaurian member of the Titanosauria, as the sister taxon to a clade formed by Chucarosaurus, Notocolossus and the Lognkosauria.

facts.statement: Bonitasaura salgadoi lived approximately 84 million years ago during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous in South America.
facts.quote: Bonitasaura salgadoi ("lagarto de La Bonita de Leonardo Salgado") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Bonitasaura de dinosaurio saurópodo saltasáurido, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 84 millones de años, en el Santoniense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Bonitasaura had a short, thin neck with robust neural arches indicating vigorous use, likely during feeding.
facts.quote: Este animal tenía un cuello delgado y corto, y arcos neurales robustos en las primeras vértebras dorsales para soportar fuertes músculos, lo que indica el uso del cuello en esfuerzos vigorosos, probablemente durante la alimentación.

facts.statement: The known subadult specimen was about 7 meters long, suggesting adults reached approximately 12 meters in length, 3 meters in height, and 5 tons in weight.
facts.quote: El ejemplar encontrado es un subadulto que habría medido cerca de 7 metros, por lo que se estima que el adulto habría medido alrededor de 12 metros de largo y 3 de alto, con un peso de 5 toneladas.

facts.statement: Bonitasaura had small, continuously replacing front teeth and a smooth posterior bone blade acting as a guillotine.
facts.quote: Los dientes en la parte anterior eran pequeños que se reemplazaban continuamente (uno funcionaba y ya había tres más esperando salir), y tenía una lisa cuchilla de hueso posterior que hacía las veces de guillotina.

facts.statement: Apesteguía described Bonitasaura in mid-2004 based on a partial adult skeleton found in a small area of fluvial sandstone.
facts.quote: Los restos, consisten en un esqueleto parcial de un adulto hallados en un área de arenisca fluvial pequeña, incluyen una quijada inferior con los dientes, las vértebras parciales y los huesos del miembro, fue descrito por Apesteguía en una comunicación corta en mediados de 2004.

facts.statement: Sebastián Apesteguía, Pablo Gallina, and Jorge González located the fossil site following directions from 98-year-old Doña Tica.
facts.quote: Apesteguía, con el entonces estudiante Pablo Gallina y el paleoartista Jorge González, siguió las indicaciones de Doña Tica de 98 años de edad, que habían dirigido a los viajeros durante los años 20 al sitio de fosilización del Bonitasaura.

facts.statement: Bonitasaura helps clarify that Antarctosaurus is included within titanosaurians rather than being a chimera of a titanosaurian body and a diplodocoid jaw.
facts.quote: Este hallazgo también aclara en algunos aspectos problemáticos de Antarctosaurus, visto a veces como una quimera de un cráneo y un postcráneo de un titanosaurio y la quijada de un diplodócido, según Jacobs en 1993, hoy es incluido dentro de los titanosaurios.

facts.statement: Bonitasaura is classified within the family Saltasauridae.
Bonitasaura lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The lower jaw had a distinctive, sharp ridge immediately behind a reduced set of teeth. This ridge supported in life a sharp, beak-like keratin sheath that probably paired with a similar structure in the upper jaw.
